dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:2401.text: The bird 烏鸔. From 鳥; 暴 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2402.text: It calls in the nine marshes, its voice heard in heaven. From 鳥; 隺 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2403.text: The white egret. From 鳥; 路 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2404.text: The bird 鴻鵠. From 鳥; 告 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2405.text: The bird 鴻鵠. From 鳥; 江 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2406.text: The bird 禿𪀖. From 鳥; 尗 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2407.text: The mandarin duck, 鴛鴦. From 鳥; 夗 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2408.text: The mandarin duck, 鴛鴦. From 鳥; 央 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2409.text: The bird 鵽鳩. From 鳥; 叕 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2410.text: The goose 蔞鵝. From 鳥; 坴 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2411.text: The goose 鴚鵝. From 鳥; 可 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2412.text: The goose 鴚鵝. From 鳥; 我 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2413.text: A goose, 䳘. From 鳥 and 人; 厂 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2414.text: The duck 舒鳧. From 鳥; 敄 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2415.text: A kind of duck. From 鳥; 殹 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “Ducks and 鷖 at the fish weir.”

shuowen:2416.text: 𪃈𪇷, a kind of duck. From 鳥; 契 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2417.text: The bird 𪃈𪇷. From 鳥; 辥 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2418.text: A waterbird. From 鳥; 蒙 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2419.text: A bird that knows when rain is coming. From 鳥; 矞 supplies the sound. The Record of Rites says: “Those who know heavenly patterns wear 鷸 feathers on their caps.”

shuowen:2420.text: The bird 𪇊鷈. From 鳥; 辟 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2421.text: The bird 𪇊鷈. From 鳥; 虒 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2422.text: The bird 𪈒鷀. From 鳥; 盧 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2423.text: The bird 𪈒鷀. From 鳥; 兹 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2424.text: The bird 鷀. From 鳥; 壹 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2425.text: The bird 𪀐绉. From 鳥; 乏 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2426.text: The bird 𪀐绉. From 鳥; 皀 supplies the sound. [The recorded headword 绉 does not match the described formation.]

shuowen:2427.text: A bird whose flesh protrudes a foot at the breast. From 鳥; 𠤏 supplies the sound. [The phrase 肉出尺𦛹 is uncertain.]

shuowen:2428.text: The bird 𪄉𪆫. From 鳥; 渠 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2429.text: A water owl. From 鳥; 區 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2430.text: A bird. From 鳥; 犮 supplies the sound. Pronounced like 撥.

shuowen:2431.text: A bird. From 鳥; 庸 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2432.text: A bird. From 鳥; 兒 supplies the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Six 鶃 flew backward.”

shuowen:2433.text: 鴺胡, namely 污澤. From 鳥; 夷 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2434.text: The bird 天狗. From 鳥; 立 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2435.text: The bird 麋鴰. From 鳥; 倉 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2436.text: The bird 麋鴰. From 鳥; 𠯑 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2437.text: The bird 𪁉𪂴. From 鳥; 交 supplies the sound. Another name is 𪁉𪈒.

shuowen:2438.text: The bird 𪁉𪂴. From 鳥; 青 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2439.text: The bird 𪁉𪂴. From 鳥; 幵 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2440.text: The bird 𪈁鴜. From 鳥; 箴 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2441.text: The bird 𪈁鴜. From 鳥; 此 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2442.text: An eagle, 雕. From 鳥; 敦 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “Neither eagle nor hawk.”

shuowen:2443.text: A bird of prey. From 鳥; 屰 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2444.text: An owl. From 鳥; 閒 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2445.text: A bird of prey. From 鳥; 䍃 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2446.text: 白鷢, the bird 王鴡. From 鳥; 厥 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2447.text: The bird 王鴡. From 鳥; 且 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2448.text: 鸛專, namely 畐蹂. Like a magpie, with a short tail; when shot at, it takes the arrow in its beak and shoots it at people. From 鳥; 雚 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2449.text: The bird 鷐風. From 鳥; 亶 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2450.text: The bird 鷐風. From 鳥; 晨 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2451.text: A bird that strikes and kills. From 鳥; 執 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2452.text: The appearance of a 鸇 in flight. From 鳥; 穴 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “Swiftly flies that 晨風.”

shuowen:2453.text: A bird. From 鳥; abbreviated 榮 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “Brilliant are its feathers.”

shuowen:2454.text: The myna, 鴝鵒. From 鳥; 句 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2455.text: The myna, 鴝鵒. From 鳥; 谷 supplies the sound. Anciently mynas did not cross the Ji River.

shuowen:2456.text: A red pheasant. From 鳥; 敝 supplies the sound. The Rites of Zhou says: “The high dignitary wears the pheasant-patterned robe and crown.”

shuowen:2457.text: 鵔鸃, the pheasant 鷩. From 鳥; 夋 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2458.text: The bird 鵔鸃. From 鳥; 義 supplies the sound. In early Qin and Han, palace attendants wore caps with 鵔鸃 feathers.

shuowen:2459.text: A kind of pheasant, a foolish bird. From 鳥; abbreviated 𨗁 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2460.text: Resembles a pheasant; found in Shangdang. From 鳥; 曷 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2461.text: A bird resembling 鶡 but blue-green, found among the Qiang. From 鳥; 介 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2462.text: 鸚䳇, a bird able to speak. From 鳥; 嬰 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2463.text: The parrot 鸚䳇. From 鳥; 母 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2464.text: A long-tailed pheasant that calls while running. For the imperial carriage its feathers make a 防釳 ornament attached to a horse's head. From 鳥; 喬 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2465.text: A female pheasant's call. From 鳥; 唯 supplies the sound. The Odes says: “The pheasant calls 鷕.”

shuowen:2466.text: A mouse-shaped bird that flies, runs and suckles its young. From 鳥; 畾 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2467.text: A plump pheasant with a 鶾 voice. From 鳥; 倝 supplies the sound. At Lu's suburban sacrifice a red chicken is invoked: “With this 鶾 voice and red feathers, remove the lord of Lu's fault.” [The precise vocal description is uncertain.]

shuowen:2468.text: The bird 雇. From 鳥; 安 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2469.text: A poisonous bird. From 鳥; 冘 supplies the sound. Also called 運日.

shuowen:2470.text: A young bird fed by its parents after hatching. From 鳥; 𣪊 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2471.text: A bird's sound. From 鳥 and 口.

shuowen:2472.text: The appearance of flight. From 鳥; abbreviated 寒 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2473.text: The appearance of birds gathering. Another explanation: a manner of flight. From 鳥; 分 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2474.text: 鷓鴣, the name of a bird. From 鳥; 庶 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2475.text: The bird 鷓鴣. From 鳥; 古 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2476.text: The duck 鶩, commonly called 鴨. From 鳥; 甲 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2477.text: 谿𪀦, a waterbird. From 鳥; 式 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2478.text: A filial bird. A pictograph. Confucius said: “烏 is 𥃳呼.” Taking its assistance in vocal breath, it is used in 烏呼, an exclamation. All graphs in this category contain 烏. [The quoted gloss is difficult.]

shuowen:2480.text: The yellow 焉 bird, found along the Yangtze and Huai. A pictograph. As for these graphs: 朋 belongs to feathered creatures; 烏 is the bird in the sun; 舄 knows the whereabouts of the Grand Year; 燕 marks the season for seeking offspring and builds nests avoiding wu and ji. Because these are esteemed, all are pictographs. 焉 is so too.

shuowen:2481.text: A kind of winnowing basket, an implement for pushing away and discarding things. A pictograph. All graphs in this category contain 𠦒. Guan Pu's explanation.

shuowen:2482.text: A hunting net. From 𠦒, depicting its shape. Fine or small. Some say 甶 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2483.text: To discard and remove. From 廾 pushing 𠦒 to discard 釆. Guan Pu explains: what resembles rice but is not rice is the character 矢. [The final identification is uncertain.]

shuowen:2484.text: To discard. From 廾 pushing 𠦒 to cast something away, and from 𠫓; 𠫓 is a reversed child.

shuowen:2485.text: Timbers stacked crosswise. It depicts opposed, intersecting forms. All graphs in this category contain 冓.

shuowen:2486.text: Twice in one undertaking. From abbreviated 冓.

shuowen:2487.text: To raise together. From 爪 and abbreviated 冓.

shuowen:2488.text: Small. It depicts a newborn child. All graphs in this category contain 幺.

shuowen:2489.text: Young. From 幺 and 力.

shuowen:2490.text: Fine or minute. From 幺; 麻 supplies the sound.

shuowen:2491.text: Minute. From two 幺. All graphs in this category contain 𢆶.

shuowen:2492.text: Hidden. From 𢆶 within 山; 𢆶 also supplies the sound.

shuowen:2493.text: Slight; perilous. From 𢆶 and 戍. 戍 means guarding with weapons; something slight yet guarded by weapons is dangerous.

shuowen:2494.text: Single-minded, minute and cautious. From abbreviated 幺; 屮 means just appearing, and also supplies the sound. All graphs in this category contain 叀.

shuowen:2495.text: Benevolence. From 心 and 叀.

shuowen:2496.text: Obstructed and unable to proceed. From 叀, pulling and stopping something; 叀 is like restraining a horse's nose. This shares the idea of 牽.

shuowen:2497.text: Hidden and far-reaching. Black with a reddish color is 玄. It depicts something hidden entering a covering. All graphs in this category contain 玄.

shuowen:2498.text: Black. From two 玄. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Why make our water black？”

shuowen:2499.text: Black color. From 玄; abbreviated 旅 supplies the sound. For this meaning, 黸 should be used.

shuowen:2500.text: To push toward and give. It depicts mutual giving. All graphs in this category contain 予.
